title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training data.

title: Comparing Bias and Variance
text: Model A has a bias squared of $$2$$ and a variance of $$12$$, while Model B has a bias squared of $$4$$ and a variance of $$1$$. Which model has higher variance?

title: Impact of High Variance
text: A model with high variance is more likely to overfit the training data. Overfitting occurs when a model captures noise in the training data rather than the intended outputs.

title: Calculating Total Error
text: The total error of a model can be calculated as the sum of bias squared and variance. Calculate the total error for both models.

title: Conclusion on Overfitting
text: Based on the total error calculated, which model is more likely to overfit the data?
